title: Chapter 3 Quiz: Building REST APIs
description: Test your knowledge of REST principles, request mapping, parameters, request bodies, status codes, and building a CRUD API.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to retrieve a resource?
questions.explanation: GET is used to retrieve data from the server.

questions.question: REST APIs should use verbs in their URLs to indicate actions.
questions.explanation: REST uses nouns for resources; HTTP methods indicate the action.

questions.question: Which annotation is used to map a class as a REST controller?
questions.explanation: @RestController is a convenience annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody.

questions.question: The shortcut for @RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.PUT) is _________.
questions.explanation: @PutMapping is the composed annotation for handling PUT requests.

questions.question: What annotation would you use to capture a value from the URL path like `/users/5`?
questions.explanation: @PathVariable binds a URI template variable to a method parameter.

questions.question: Query parameters are part of the URL after the ? and are typically used for filtering.
questions.explanation: Query parameters are appended after ? and are ideal for optional parameters like sorting, pagination, etc.

questions.question: Which annotation tells Spring to map the HTTP request body to a Java object?
questions.explanation: @RequestBody is used to bind the request body to a method parameter.

questions.question: The HTTP status code 201 means _________.
questions.explanation: 201 Created is returned when a new resource has been successfully created.

questions.question: What class gives you full control over the response status, headers, and body?
questions.explanation: ResponseEntity allows you to set status, headers, and body explicitly.

questions.question: A DELETE endpoint should typically return a 204 No Content status.
questions.explanation: 204 No Content is standard for successful DELETE, indicating the resource was removed and no response body is needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to set a default value for a query parameter?
questions.explanation: You can set a defaultValue attribute on @RequestParam to provide a fallback value.

questions.question: To make a query parameter optional, you can set _________ to false.
questions.explanation: @RequestParam(required = false) makes the parameter optional.

questions.question: What is the correct way to map a GET endpoint that returns a list of all products?
questions.explanation: The simplest and most RESTful way is @GetMapping("/products") to retrieve all products.

questions.question: You can use @PathVariable on a method parameter that is not a String.
questions.explanation: Spring automatically converts the path variable to the parameter type (e.g., Long, Integer) if possible.

questions.question: What does the `consumes` attribute of @RequestMapping specify?
options: The content type the method returns
The content type the method accepts
questions.explanation: `consumes` restricts the media types that the method can consume from the request.

questions.question: The annotation _________ can be used on an exception class to map it to a specific HTTP status.
questions.explanation: @ResponseStatus can be placed on an exception class to define the HTTP status that should be returned when that exception is thrown.

questions.question: Which status code indicates that the server cannot find the requested resource?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found is the standard response for a non‑existent resource.

questions.question: In Spring Boot, if you don't specify a status, the default is 200 OK.
questions.explanation: If no status is explicitly set, Spring returns 200 OK for successful requests.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Location header in a 201 response?
options: To indicate the client should redirect
To provide the URL of the newly created resource
questions.explanation: The Location header in a 201 response typically contains the URI of the newly created resource.

questions.question: A _________ API is one that follows the principles of Representational State Transfer.
questions.explanation: APIs that adhere to REST principles are called RESTful APIs.
